primitives.name: Ball-Foot Alignment Operator
primitives.verbatim_quote: It should come accurately on to the outside of the foot, lacings up, long axis either parallel to the long axis of the shoe or slightly turned in.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'θ': "angle in radians between ball's long axis and shoe's long axis", 'd': "distance from foot's contact point to ball's center in meters"}
primitives.assumptions: Ball orientation is controlled by hand positioning; foot contact is modeled as a rigid body constraint.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when θ deviates beyond ±0.1 radians from ideal alignment.

layer2.mapping: GSI models alignment as a Gaussian likelihood over angular deviation; GSE encodes alignment as a deterministic state transition in kinematic chain.
layer2.telemetry: Angular deviation from target alignment measured via optical tracking.

primitives.name: Visual Tracking Stability
primitives.verbatim_quote: The eye of the kicker should be kept constantly and vigilantly on the ball.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'v_{eye}': 'eye velocity vector in m/s', 't_{fixation}': 'fixation duration in seconds'}
primitives.assumptions: Visual tracking maintains constant gaze on ball during flight phase; eye movement is bounded by saccadic latency.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Tracking fails when v_{eye} exceeds 10 m/s or t_{fixation} < 0.05s.

layer2.mapping: GSI computes tracking reliability as entropy of gaze distribution; GSE evaluates tracking robustness as temporal coherence of visual input.
layer2.telemetry: Gaze position variance and fixation duration recorded via eye-tracker.

primitives.name: Preparatory Motion Variability
primitives.verbatim_quote: Some step back with their kicking foot, then forward with the off foot, and then kick.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'s_{step}': 'step length in meters', 't_{prep}': 'preparation time in seconds'}
primitives.assumptions: Step sequence is stochastic but bounded; motion timing is synchronized with ball trajectory.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Variability exceeds acceptable range when s_{step} varies > 0.1m or t_{prep} > 0.3s.

layer2.mapping: GSI treats step variability as a random walk in action space; GSE models it as a policy distribution over motion states.
layer2.telemetry: Step length and timing variance from motion capture data.
